speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand these episodes of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing, can you describe exactly what happens right before an episode starts? Also, how long do these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does he have any history of head trauma, high fever, or seizures in his family? I would also like to know if these episodes occur during sleep or only when he is awake. REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG findings and your description of an aura with post-ictal confusion strongly suggest focal seizures originating from the right temporal lobe. To confirm the structural cause and rule out other abnormalities, I need to visualize the brain tissue. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with epilepsy protocol

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI is normal, this points to idiopathic focal epilepsy rather than a structural cause. I will request visual examples of typical seizure semiology to further confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Doctor
text: The visual confirmation of the automated hand gestures and post-ictal confusion, combined with the right temporal EEG spikes, confirms the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Right temporal lobe epilepsy
